reconcile.note: Henry notes that casting out devils in Christ's name never proved genuine faith, citing Judas himself as an exorcist who was nonetheless lost.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Who can cast out devils in the name of Jesus?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/devils.html) (2013).

sides.snippet: John said to him, \"Teacher, we saw someone who doesn't follow us casting out demons in your name; and we forbade him, because he doesn't follow us.\"
sides.verseText: John said to him, \"Teacher, we saw someone who doesn't follow us casting out demons in your name; and we forbade him, because he doesn't follow us.\"

sides.snippet: These signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons; they will speak with new languages;
sides.verseText: These signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons; they will speak with new languages;
